definition: Affective engineering is an approach to studying or designing interactions by focusing on users’ emotional and motivational responses. In this context, it examines how features of an interaction, such as expected capability and uncertainty, shape intrinsic motivation to engage for enjoyment rather than only practical benefit.

reasons: The packet does not define “affective engineering” as an approach that focuses on users’ emotional responses; it only references an “affective engineering approach” in connection with intrinsic motivation.
Claims about “studying or designing interactions” are not explicitly supported by the packet text, which mainly describes the authors’ motivation model and experiments.

The portion about expectation of capability and uncertainty affecting intrinsic motivation to engage for fun (intrinsic motivation) is supported, but the definition contains unsupported elements (especially the emotional-focus wording).
The packet supports a study of intrinsic motivation in human–AI interaction, but it does not define affective engineering as a general approach to studying or designing interactions.
“Users’ emotional responses” is not supported by the packet; the source discusses motivation, not emotion.
The definition overgeneralizes the source’s specific model (expectation of capability and uncertainty in virtual-assistant interaction) into a broader account of the term.
